analysis:
I found no concrete security regression in the visible changes. The PR is diagnostics and recovery-heuristic only. It touches docs/provider/troubleshooting.md (lines 83 and 143), UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery.swift, and ServingReadiness.swift. It does not change routing or authorization. Those stay with the trusted coordinator (TB-011, A-016, T-053). The provider only reports status and decides when to re-register.

UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery.swift: the head side removes `connectionLacksAuthorization` (base lines 38-49). The doc comment now says only the blocked `ServingReadiness` verdict counts. The remaining `shouldReconnect` is unchanged (head lines 26-34). It keeps the 15-minute threshold plus jitter, the 30-minute to 4-hour backoff, and the idle-only (`busy`) gate. That is the availability protection against reconnect storms.

ServingReadiness.swift: only the metadata unit and a truncated patch excerpt were supplied. The excerpt shows a new `.unconfirmed` verdict. A refusal older than `refusalMaxAge` (60s) is no longer blocked, and a request routed after the latest status now counts as authorized. The excerpt also shows `statusGraceSeconds` (90s) with a note about the registration status. This can only make the local diagnostic less aggressive. It cannot grant serving permission, because the coordinator still decides routing (T-052, T-053, T-057). I could not read the full implementation, so I could not check the following:
- whether the 'routed since latest status' signal can be spoofed or confused with an unauthenticated message;
- whether callers in ProviderLoop+ServingAuthorizationRecovery.swift and the status/doctor paths handle `.unconfirmed` exhaustively (a fail-open default would be a diagnostic-trust issue);
- whether `darkbloom doctor`/`status` strictness (exit code) treats `.unconfirmed` correctly.

The docs changes match the described behavior. No new data exposure, secrets, or attack surface appear in the visible diff.
